headline: Mathematicians warn that arXiv, the website where researchers share papers before peer review, might not survive a flood of low-quality AI-made papers.
score_reason: Lowered from 5: the full article could not be checked, so the warning rests on its headline.
importance_line: Researchers who rely on arXiv to share and find new work could lose a main channel if it cannot cope with AI-made submissions, but the mathematicians' reasons, evidence and proposed fixes are not known from the headline.
summary: New Scientist reports that mathematicians are warning that arXiv, the free website where researchers post papers before peer review, might not survive a flood of low-quality AI-generated submissions, days after arXiv capped each submitter at two new papers a month, announced on 1 Oct 2026 according to The Register.
notes: New Scientist page refused (HTTP 406) and no other outlet carries this piece (Google News searches on 6 Oct 2026), so the entry rests on the headline. The earlier story it follows was read in full on The Register (2 Oct 2026): arXiv now limits each submitter to two new submissions a month, announced Thursday 1 Oct 2026, after 40,363 submissions in September 2026 against 9,869 ten years earlier. Pool follow-up of 'arXiv now limits every researcher to two paper submissions a month' (Startup Fortune, 2 Oct 2026). Score lowered by one because only the headline could be checked.
